memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Keep this Book of the Law always on your lips; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful." — Josh 1:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Joshua how to stay courageous and faithful: soak your mind in God's Word. Keep it on your lips — that is, speak it, repeat it, let it shape your conversation. Meditate on it day and night — turn it over in your mind the way you might turn a sweet over in your mouth, slowly, again and again.

Notice the purpose God gives: "so that you may be careful to do everything written in it." Meditation is not merely for warm feelings or head knowledge. It leads to obedience. We do not truly know God's Word until it changes how we live.

About "prosperous and successful" — we must read this honestly. This is God's specific assurance to Joshua for his God-given task, not a formula guaranteeing wealth for anyone who reads the Bible enough. Scripture never promises that Bible reading makes us rich. What it does promise is that God's Word, taken to heart, makes us wise, steady, and fruitful in the things that matter to God.

Jesus is the Word made flesh (John 1:14), and all Scripture ultimately points to Him (Luke 24:27). To meditate on God's Word is to draw near to Christ Himself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When do you set aside time to slowly think over God's Word, not just read it quickly?
2. Does your meditation lead to obedience, or stop at good feelings?
3. How can you keep Scripture "on your lips" throughout your ordinary day?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a hunger for Your Word. Help me not just to read it, but to meditate on it and live it out. Amen.
